Ecological Identity What Worries Me

Nov 19, 2010 • Janice Cotcher

Wastefulness I am so fortunate that I live in a country with so many resources. We really take for granted how much we have and how much we waste. Even though it takes me longer to get to school, I take the bus instead of driving my car. It saves me a lot of money and it makes me feel like I’m contributing less pollution.

I haven’t been able to convince anyone to start taking public transit. What the argument always comes down to is convenience. The bus takes longer to get to their destination. They would have to walk several blocks to/from the bus stop. Until the cost of running cars becomes to prohibitive or the transit system becomes more convenient, this is not going to change.

I admit that my own wastefulness is often due to convenience. I try to take lunch everyday but some days I run out of time in the morning and have to buy lunch at school. Other times I have to stay later at school than expected and I’m too hungry to wait until I get home. Being unprepared and having to buy food causes a lot of garbage. I need to learn to plan better for the unexpected and make time to get meals ready for school.

Overwhelmed by the problem It is a little frustrating knowing that the efforts that I currently am making are not enough. Yes, “every bit counts” but I could be doing more. I feel like I’m being pulled in all directions. Be a better teacher, be a better Christian, eat better, get in better shape, do more for the environment, spend more time with friends and family, do better in school, be better organized… My attention feels very divided. How do I prioritize? What things can I do for the environment that will cause the greatest impact?

The minds of others I need keep reminding myself that “It is hard enough to change yourself, even more difficult to change others”.

I was a little disgusted this past Earth Hour that some teenagers I know turned on VERY LIGHT in the house then bragged about it. OK, I know, maybe it upset me more than it should have. I know they were just doing it for a laugh from their friends but it irked me. It is one thing to not participate in Earth Hour but it is an entirely different thing to mock those who do. There was a heated but futile exchange about wastefulness that I eventually dropped because I knew that I nothing I said was going to change their mind. It left me so discouraged that youth today either don’t think there is a problem with the environment or don’t think there is anything they can do about it. This worries me as an educator as to how to deal with situations like this in the classroom.

How my environment effects my health In many ways, my allergies are the worst they have ever been. I know that my allergies are inherited but I feel like my environment makes them worse. I worry that exposure to harsh chemicals over time has weakened my immune system or made it hyper-sensitive to my environment. Besides living in a bubble, what can I do? There is so much confusing information out there about what is harmful and what is good for you, how can I make a plan of action? Is there anything I can do to help? Will cost prohibit me for making the necessary changes?

Future children As of right now, I do not know if I will ever have children but I’d like to. Sometimes I worry about my future children inheriting my allergic predisposition. What kind of world will I be bringing them into? Will I be too ill too often to care for them? Will my own experiences help prevent a lot of them problems I’ve had?
